name: Jatniel
title: Gatekeeper at the temple
summary: Jatniel was one of the gatekeepers who served at God's house in Jerusalem during King David's time. He was a son of Meshelemiah (also called Shelemiah), a Korahite who had responsibility for guarding the sanctuary. His role was to guard the entrances to the tabernacle and later the temple.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as Gatekeeper
keyEvents.description: Jatniel was appointed as one of the gatekeepers at the house of the Lord, as part of the Levitical service organized under King David.

keyEvents.title: Service Among the Sons of Meshelemiah
keyEvents.description: Jatniel is mentioned as the fourth son of Meshelemiah, a Korahite, and served faithfully in his assigned role as gatekeeper at the sanctuary.

keyEvents.title: Organization of the Gatekeeping Service
keyEvents.description: King David organized the gatekeeping service by casting lots, through which Jatniel and his family received their assigned watches and responsibilities.

keyEvents.title: Part of the Levitical Arrangement
keyEvents.description: As a Korahite, Jatniel was part of a long tradition of Levites entrusted with guarding God's sanctuary, an arrangement that dates back to the time of Moses.
